subject.title: fix(agents): hard-deadline runtime auth refresh to prevent gateway deadlock

question: Should this PR require side-effect-safe cancellation or late-write guards before merging the auth deadline backstops?
rationale: The patch targets a real availability failure, but the current timeout-race design changes auth-provider and session-state ownership in ways green tests do not prove safe.

options.title: Require side-effect-safe timeout ownership
options.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime-auth operations cannot persist credentials or mutate active auth state after their ownership has ended.

options.title: Accept the deadline-only mitigation
options.body: Merge the current patch as an availability mitigation while explicitly owning the late-write and budget-headroom risks.

options.title: Pause for an auth-owner redesign
options.body: Hold the PR until the auth concurrency design and real recovery proof are owner-approved.

recommendation.title: Require side-effect-safe timeout ownership
recommendation.body: Block merge until timed-out OAuth and runtime-auth operations cannot persist credentials or mutate active auth state after their ownership has ended.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history across the embedded runtime auth and OAuth manager surfaces changed here.
